No misfortune occurs for him, and all prosperities come to pass, when incense is offered with devotion before me every month without ceasing. (31)
Incense bestows beauty; incense is the supreme purifier. It is the divine essence of the forest trees, the highest purifier, and pure. (32)
Hereafter, I shall proclaim the supreme majesty of the lamp; by performing which, a person goes to Vaikuṇṭha—of this there is no doubt.
Whoever performs the *ārārtika* ceremony provided with many wicks and accompanied by offerings of *ghṛtapūra*, shall indeed dwell in heaven for ten million *kalpas*.
He who beholds the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) before me in the month of Sahas (Mārgaśīrṣa) shall indeed become a Brahmin for seven births, and in the end, attain the supreme state.
O best of the twice-born, he who performs the *ārārtika* rite with camphor before me with devotion shall enter my eternal abode.
O son, whatever worship of mine has been performed deficient in mantra or deficient in ritual action—all that becomes complete when the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) is performed.
He who offers a lamp with camphor during the month of Sahas (Mārgaśīrṣa) attains the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice and uplifts his entire lineage. || 38 ||
One should offer a lamp before me, before the twice-born, and at a crossroads; such a man becomes intelligent, endowed with knowledge, and possessed of keen vision. (39)
If a man lights a lamp with either ghee or oil before me in the month of Sahas (Mārgaśīrṣa), listen to the fruit of his merit. || 40 ||
Having abandoned all evil, resembling a thousand suns, he is glorified in my world by means of a luminous celestial chariot.
Therefore, a wise person should offer a lamp with every effort; he who, having offered it, should cause it harm, will certainly fall into hell.
O best of the twice-born, that sinner who steals a lamp out of greed or hatred is born as both mute and blind because of that theft of the lamp. (43)

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Lamp," in the Mārgaśīrṣa-māhātmya, within the Dialogue between Brahmā and Viṣṇu, in the second Vaiṣṇava-khaṇḍa of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

Brahmā said: O Lord, O Master, tell me truly the procedure for the food offering (naivedya); how many kinds of food are desired, and what are the side dishes (vyañjana) and so forth, without omission? || 1 ||
The Blessed Lord said: "Well asked by you, my child; it is most pleasing to me. I shall describe to you in its entirety the food, drink, condiments, and so forth."
First, a golden vessel; in its absence, a silver one; and in its absence, a broad and very beautiful vessel made of palāśa wood. || 3 ||
O sinless one, hundreds of small bowls should indeed be arranged all around the vessel; in their midst, auspicious side dishes consisting of various fruits should be placed. || 4 ||
Milk-rice, resembling the moon, together with sugar, in a vessel; cooked rice, resembling a white water-lily; and auspicious mung beans with the luster of glass.
It was filled with various side dishes arranged in three rows, along with lime juice, camphor, and fruits and roots.
And at that time, hundreds of various preparations should be made for my meal; grapes should be mixed with mangoes and karamarda fruits to make them auspicious.
Black pepper, long pepper, fresh ginger, cardamom, and camphor, combined and boiled together, shall be prepared as soups for me at my meals by the hundreds.
Likewise, luscious morsels filled with hundreds of fruits and perfumed with the fragrance of various flowers should be prepared; they are dear to me in the month of Sahasī. (9)
The *maṇḍakas* are round, beautiful, and uniform everywhere like a drop; they are prepared with boiled milk mixed with sugar.
O child, within that splendid kacola vessel filled with excellent food mixed with honey-colored cow's milk, there stood something of golden luster.
Indeed, well-scented ghee should be given with affection for my meal; it should be served there in a vessel of wheat, shining with a decorative crescent moon design.
Sauvāhlikas, pūrikās, those with a hundred holes, and veṣṭikas; likewise, cakes and milk—one should prepare these various kinds.
There were gems known as *sūtra*, *mālatī* flowers and the like, and beautiful *parpaṭas* and *varpaṭas* produced from *māṣa* and *kūṣmāṇḍa*.
In the month of Sahas, you should prepare nine kinds of beautiful *vaṭaka* cakes for me; these auspicious ones should be filled with two types of *jātī* and *marīca* in a *droṇa* measure. (15)
Filled with well-prepared salt and exceedingly pure oil, they possess the hue of saffron; yet, being devoid of oil, they appear like wicked men who are full of flaws.
Some were mixed with curd and milk, some were derived from tamarind and mango; some were mixed with grape juice, and likewise some were mixed with sugarcane juice. || 17 ||
Vaṭakas containing mustard seeds placed in water, as well as others with sugar and four other types of juices, are considered to be of nine kinds. (18)
With pieces of coconut combined with a hundred cloves, along with *vajraprabhā*, *anukaṇikā*, *cārabīja*, and *sukhārika*. (19)
Those *pheṇikās*, well-stirred in a cauldron with ghee, milk, sugar, and other ingredients, are glossy and as delightful as *kṛsara* mixed with sugar and other substances. (20)
Indeed, at the Parākīkā shrines, cooked *polikās* prepared by Candra should be offered; furthermore, *modakas* produced from *cāra* seeds should be made there.
Others should be made with sugar, while others are prepared with milk; still others are made with coconut fruits, and others are made from tree exudations.
One should have other auspicious modakas made with badāma, sesame seeds, and kaṇabīja seeds; such and other varieties should be prepared for my satisfaction. (23)
The bulb of the mocanī plant which destroys hemorrhoids, as well as fresh karamardaka, nāriṅga, ciñciṇīka, and the fruit of kaṅkola. || 24 ||
The auspicious ten-spoked [wheel], the three cities-born, the nimba fruit, the lotus stalk, the tinduka fruit, the clove, the bilva fruit, the tilaka, and the lutī. (25)
Bark, bamboo, kārīra, as well as kāyaphala, bala, grapes, mango fruit, and the lovely fruit of the kaṇṭakinī; || 26 ||

The fruit of the dhātrī, the fruit produced from vinegar (śuktibhava), as well as the ambāḍava fruit, the fruit of the plantain (raṃbhā), long pepper (pippalī), and beautiful black peppers (marīca). || 27 ||
Well-pierced with pure mustard oil and salt, and likewise pierced with black mustard, it remains in a jar for three years. (28)
O giver of honor, such side dishes as these should be prepared during the month of Sahas, for they truly bring me delight. (29)
If there should be an inability to provide such a feast, then one should act in this manner; listen to me as I describe it in brief. (30)
One who gives one *laḍḍūka*, one *ghṛtapūra*, two *phenas*, three *kokarasas*, sixteen *maṇḍakas* soaked in ghee, and eight *vaṭas*, shall not see hell.

One āḍhaka of milk that has been stored for a very long time, sixteen palas of candied sugar with the luster of the moon, one pala of ghee, one pala of honey, two karṣas of black pepper, and half a pala of ginger—or else half a pala each of these four. (32)
To that man who prepares this auspicious *rasavatī*, white as camphor powder, contained in a vessel and rubbed with soft hands by a woman upon a smooth cloth—to him, I grant all his desires. (33)

Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Ritual for Food Offerings," in the *Mārgaśīrṣa-māhātmya* (The Greatness of the Month of Mārgaśīrṣa) within the dialogue between Brahmā and Viṣṇu, in the second section (*Vaiṣṇava-khaṇḍa*) of the *Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa*, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Brahmā said: O Father, O Lord, what should be done by men after the offering of food (naivedya)? Tell me truly everything that ought to be performed during the month of Sahas (Mārgaśīrṣa). || 1 ||

The Blessed Lord said: Then, having given water scented with camphor for the guest who has finished eating, one should offer water for sipping (ācamana), betel leaf, sandalwood paste, and water for washing the hands.
Then one should offer a handful of flowers and, with devotion, present a mirror; thereafter, the lustration (nīrājana) should be performed, using camphor if one has the means.
Having offered his crown and other ornaments, O wise one, he then, O illustrious one, provided the royal umbrella and the chowries.
Having meditated upon the Lord whose form is dark and beautiful, with a face radiant with grace, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times and praise the Master with hymns.
A garland made of conch and silver, and especially one of gold, as well as those made of auspicious lotus seeds, coral, gems, and pearls.
A rosary fashioned from indrākṣa beads, as well as one made from the joints of fingers, and a rosary made of putrajīva seeds are indeed recommended for the rite of recitation.
Neither walking nor laughing, nor looking to the side; neither treading one foot with the other, nor likewise with his hands placed upon his head.
A wise man, remaining awake, should recite my mantra with an undistracted mind; he should not speak during the time of recitation, nor during vows, fire-offerings, worship, and so forth.

Recitation performed in one's home yields a single-fold merit; in a cow-pen it becomes ten-fold; on a riverbank one should know it to be a hundred-fold; and in a fire-sanctuary it is ten times more than that.

"At holy places and the like, the merit may be a thousandfold, but in my presence it is infinite. Having performed this in the month of Sahas, he who then performs a circumambulation [attains the same]. (11)
Reciting the Thousand Names, or even just the Name alone, one obtains at every step the merit of [giving away] the earth consisting of seven islands. (12)
A single circumambulation performed with devotion always burns away the sins of a day; by him, the earth with its seven continents has been circumambulated.
Three circumambulations of me destroy the sin produced over seven days; they likewise instantly destroy the sin of ten days within the body.
By him who has performed twenty-one circumambulations with devotion, sins such as the killing of a fetus are destroyed at that very moment.
He who has performed one hundred and eight circumambulations with devotion has thereby offered all sacrifices accompanied by the most excellent sacrificial fees.
He circumambulated the earth that many times; likewise, he performed circumambulations of his mother and circumambulations of the earth, the sustainer of beings. (17)
These three are considered equal to the Śāligrāma stone: a single prostration with a staff and seven circumambulations performed together.
These two are equal, or rather, the falling of the staff is superior; for he who always performs the falling of the staff during my circumambulation [attains the greater merit]. (19)
Especially by performing it for one month, he shall dwell in heaven until the end of the kalpa; thereafter, O dear one, he is born as a universal monarch (cakravartin).
Through the recitation of the Thousand Names, one becomes long-lived, wealthy, an enjoyer of pleasures, a giver of charity, and a lover of dharma; the threefold sin committed shall be destroyed.
Now, what is the use of much speaking? Listen to my secret, O son: my incomparable affection truly lies with the name Dāmodara.
My mother Yaśodā gave me this name based on a quality, when I caused the bursting of a vessel of curds in Gokula.
Then Yaśodā bound me firmly with a rope to the mortar; from that time forth, my name became celebrated as Dāmodara.
He who, having become pure at sunrise, recites "Namo Dāmodarāya" three thousand times every day with a well-composed mind; || 25 ||

The wise one should continue this for as long as three hundred thousand [recitations]; then he should perform the libation (tarpaṇa) and the fire-oblation (havana), and feed the Brahmins in a tenth part of that number. || 26 ||
Thus, to whoever performs this with devotion, I grant their desire: wealth, grain, as well as a wife, sons, and whatever else is desired.
"I have spoken this out of the Three Truths; believe me, O Mahāmati! O son, this king of mantras has been revealed by me out of compassion. (28)
Reciting "To Dāmodara," O son, one should constantly perform circumambulation, as well as prostrations like a staff, endowed with all eight limbs.
With the two feet, the two hands, the two knees, the chest, the head, as well as the mind, speech, and sight, a prostration is called *aṣṭāṅga* (eight-limbed).
Placing my head at your feet and clasping one another with our arms, I have come to you for refuge; O Lord, protect me, who am terrified by the ocean of the jaws of death.
Afterwards, O child, having respectfully placed upon your head the remainder given by me, you should speak thus for the sake of completing my worship.
O Janārdana, O God, whatever has been worshipped by me—whether deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, or deficient in devotion—may that become complete for me. (33)
Accompanied by the sound of the mṛdaṅga drum and perfectly joined with the syllable Om (praṇava), dancing should be performed in this manner during the month of Sahas; it bestows merit upon men.
O Four-faced One, song, instrumental music, dance, and likewise the recitation of sacred texts are always dear to me at the time of worship. (35)
And in the absence of song, instrumental music, and the like, O son, [recite] my Thousand Names, the King of Hymns, and likewise the Liberation of Gajendra.
Recollection, singing, and praise are considered to be fivefold; O fortunate one, this "Fivefold Praise" is supremely pleasing to me. (37)
If one indeed drinks the water from the feet [of the Lord] originating from the Śāligrāma, what need is there for the consumption of thousands of *pañcagavya*? (38)
The man who drinks even as much as a drop of water from a Śāligrāma stone shall never again drink his mother’s milk; such a person becomes a partaker of liberation.

No impurity whatsoever shall exist for those who place the water from his feet upon their heads and who partake of it as a sacred draught, whether in the case of birth or even in the case of death. (40)
Even at the time of death, he who offers this water at the feet attains a good rebirth, even if he has been excluded from virtuous conduct.
That man who drinks what is undrinkable, who eats what is not to be eaten, who indeed approaches those who should not be approached, and who is of sinful conduct; || 42 ||
He too becomes instantly purified immediately by holding the water from the feet; the water at the feet is superior to the Cāndrāyaṇa and the Pādakṛcchra penances.
Whether it be agallochum, saffron, camphor, or even an ointment, once it has come into contact with the water from my feet, it indeed becomes the purifier of purifiers.
O best of Brahmins, even water that has been purified by the gaze [of a holy man] removes the sins of men; how much more so the water from their feet? (45)
"You are my beloved eldest son, and especially dear to me; for that reason, I have told you everything, including the secret that resides within me. (46)

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Conclusion of the Ritual of Worship, its Valedictory Rite (Udyāpana), and the Exposition of its Fruits," in the Mārgaśīrṣa-māhātmya, within the Dialogue between Brahmā and Viṣṇu, in the second Vaiṣṇava-khaṇḍa of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Brahmā said: O Lord, creator of all beings, please tell me out of compassion the entire greatness of Ekādaśī and the ritual procedure for its forms.
The Blessed Lord said: Listen, O tiger among the twice-born, to this story that destroys sin; by hearing it, even sins such as the killing of a Brahmin go to their dissolution.
In the city of Kāmpilya, there was a king known as Vīrabāhu; he was truthful, had conquered his anger, was a knower of Brahman, and was devoted to me.
That man was possessed of good character, compassionate, handsome, and strong; he was devoted to the devotees of the Lord and always took delight in my stories. || 4 ||
He was always devoted to my stories, always fond of staying awake, a donor, learned, patient by nature, valiant, and one who had conquered his senses.
He shall be victorious and skilled in battle, equal to Kubera in prosperity, possessed of sons and cattle, and likewise devoted to his own wife.
His wife was Kāntimatī, peerless on earth in beauty; she was a devoted wife, a great saintly woman, and always intent on devotion to me.
Together with her, the large-eyed youth enjoyed the earth; O mighty-armed one, he knew no other deity except for me alone.
One day, O son, the great sage Bhāradvāja arrived at the house of that high-souled Vīrabāhu.
Seeing the great sage Bhāradvāja arrived from afar, he then offered him a welcome and presented the arghya according to the prescribed rites.
The lord of the earth himself prepared a seat; having bowed with supreme devotion, he stood before the best of sages.
The king said: Today my birth has become fruitful; today my day has become fruitful; today my kingdom has become fruitful; today my home has become fruitful. (12)
O brahmin-sage, Janārdana, the Supreme Soul, is pleased with me, since you, the best of yogis, have come to my home today.
"I am liberated today from ten million sins because I have been beheld by you; my kingdom, prosperity, elephants, and horses are offered by me unto you. (14)
"You are a Vaiṣṇava, O best of sages; there is nothing that I cannot give to you. To a Vaiṣṇava, even a single cowrie shell is equal to the entirety of Mount Meru. (15)
"O best of the twice-born, it has been told to me by the Brahmins that for him in whose house a devotee of Viṣṇu does not come, that day is indeed fruitless."
"And whoever are devotees of Viṣṇu, all castes and the twice-born—this was told to me by Gārgya, Gautama, and Sumantu. (17)
Those men who are not devoted to Hṛṣīkeśa are indeed Piśācas; they are smeared with great sins who eat on the day of Hari.
Whatever fruit is proclaimed by the wise to be gained from thousands of Śiva-vows and tens of millions of Saura and Brāhma vows, that same fruit is obtained in a single day of Hari.
O best of Brahmins, both the lunar day sacred to Brahmā and that sacred to Śaṅkara maintain their pride only so long as my beloved Dvādaśī does not arrive.
O best of Brahmins, the stars possess such power only so long as the moon has not risen; likewise, a lunar day possesses its full efficacy only so long as the twelfth day (Dvādaśī) has not arrived.
"O great sage, it was told of old by Nārada and Vasiṣṭha in my presence: 'You are the knower of all the dharmas of the Vaiṣṇavas. (22)
Bhāradvāja said: Well asked, O illustrious one, for you are indeed a devotee of Viṣṇu. Blessed is that earth with its good offspring, since you protect it, O protector of the land.

One should not dwell in that kingdom where the king is not a devotee of Viṣṇu; rather, dwelling in a forest hermitage or at a sacred ford is better than living in a kingdom where there is no Vaiṣṇava.
Wherever a king devoted to the Lord governs the earth, that kingdom should be considered Vaikuṇṭha itself, free from all sin.
Just as a body deprived of sight, or women deprived of a husband, so too is a kingdom that is not Vaiṣṇava when the twelfth lunar day is joined with the tenth.

O protector of the earth, just as a son who does not support his mother and father [is blameworthy], so too is a kingdom that is devoid of Vaiṣṇavas when the twelfth lunar day is joined with the tenth.
Just as a king devoid of charity, a Brahmin who sells liquids, or the twelfth lunar day joined with the tenth, so too is a kingdom that is not Vaiṣṇava.
Just as an elephant deprived of its tusks, or a bird deprived of its wings, so too is a kingdom devoid of Vaiṣṇavas when the twelfth lunar day is joined with the tenth.

Just as the Vedas and other scriptures are for the sake of receiving gifts, and good deeds are for the sake of wealth, so too is a kingdom that is not Vaiṣṇava like a twelfth lunar day joined with the tenth.

Just as the twilight ritual is deficient without darbha grass, just as a śrāddha is without a sacrificial fee, so too is a kingdom without Vaiṣṇavas, even if it occurs on the twelfth lunar day when joined with the tenth.
Just as a Śūdra who wears a topknot and drinks the milk of a tawny cow, so too is a kingdom that is not Vaiṣṇava when the twelfth lunar day is joined with the tenth.

A Śūdra who approaches a Brāhmaṇa woman, one who steals gold, a corrupter of dharma, a twelfth lunar day joined with the tenth, and likewise a kingdom that is not Vaiṣṇava—[these are causes of downfall].
O best of men, just as trees such as the *hari* and *sūrya* are destroyed when cut down, so too is a kingdom that is not devoted to Viṣṇu ruined when the twelfth lunar day is joined with the tenth.
Just as an oblation devoid of mantras, or like milk from a cow that has miscarried its calf, so too is a kingdom that is not Vaiṣṇava when the twelfth day is joined with the tenth.
Just as a widow with her hair unbound observes a vow while abstaining from bathing, so too is a kingdom that is not devoted to Viṣṇu when its twelfth day is joined with the tenth.
He is called a king by the virtuous who is devoted to Madhusūdana; his kingdom prospers constantly, and he, along with his subjects, becomes happy. (37)
O King, my sight has become fruitful because you have been beheld by me; today my speech has also become fruitful, for it speaks with you. (38)
Indeed, it is heard that one must travel even a great distance to where a Vaiṣṇava resides; for by the mere sight of him, there arises merit equal to that born from bathing at a sacred ford (tīrtha).
O King, you have been seen by me as one who is pure and devoted to Viṣṇu; may it be well with you, I shall depart; be happy, O lord of men. (40)
In the meantime, the best of sages, Bhāradvāja, the preeminent among all yogis, was saluted by Queen Kāntimatī.
"O lady of beautiful hips, may you never suffer widowhood; O auspicious one, may your devotion to your own husband be firm, and may your devotion to Keśava always remain unwavering. (42)
In the meantime, the king, gladdening the great sage Bhāradvāja with words as deep as the roar of a thundercloud, spoke to him.
The king said: "How did my great fortune come to be? What was done by me in a previous birth? Tell me everything, O best of sages, if you have compassion for me. (44)
How have I obtained this kingdom, free from all thorns? Indeed, I have a most excellent and virtuous son, and a beloved wife who is exceedingly charming. (45)
With my mind fixed on you and my life-breaths dedicated to you, I was contemplating Janārdana: "O Sage, who am I? How did this [state] come to be? And what dharma have I performed? (46)
Moreover, O sage, what has been done by this lovely-limbed wife of mine, and by what merit have I obtained such prosperity as is very difficult to attain in the world of mortals? (47)
Indeed, all the rulers of the earth without exception abide under my command; likewise, my prowess is unimpeded and my body enjoys perfect health. (48)
O Sage, no one can endure my vast splendor either; today I wish to make a vow so that this blameless woman may be restored.
"O Brahmin, what meritorious deed was performed by me in a previous birth? Thus questioned by the king, [the sage] related the activities of his former life.
And he reflected in his mind for a very long time upon the conduct of his own wife and the cause of his prosperity, which had arisen from yoga.
O King, this conduct of your former birth is known; O royal sage, listen as I relate it to you along with that of your wife. (52)
Bhāradvāja said: Listen, O protector of the earth, to the entirety of that action of which this is the fruit: you were once born of the Śūdra caste, devoted to the injury of living beings. (53)
An atheist, of wicked conduct, a violator of another's wife, ungrateful, ill-mannered, and utterly devoid of proper behavior. (54)
This wife of yours, who was long-eyed even from before, has had nothing other than you as her companion in deed, thought, or speech. (55)
"Being a devoted wife and highly fortunate, she constantly serves you; even so, she does not harbor any wicked intent toward you. (56)
Abandoned by your friends and kinsmen, you who committed evil deeds, even the wealth that had been accumulated by your ancestors went to ruin.
O Lord of the World, when your wealth was lost, you remained desirous of its fruit; yet, due to the ripening of past karma, your agriculture has gone to waste.
Then, when his wealth was exhausted and he had been abandoned by his kinsmen, that virtuous and passionate woman did not desert you, even though she herself was wasting away.
Broken away from all desires, you went to the lonely forest; having slain numerous living beings, you made them food for yourself. (60)
O King, as you thus engaged in that sinful conduct upon the earth together with your wife, many years passed away.
On another day, O King, the great sage Devaśarman, the best of the twice-born, having lost his way, knew neither the cardinal nor the intermediate directions.
O Lord of the Earth, excessively afflicted by hunger and thirst at midday when the sun was blazing, he fell into the middle of the forest, having lost his way.
And compassion arose within you, O King, upon seeing the aged Brāhmaṇa afflicted by suffering; indeed, you took him by the hand. (64)
O King, when he had fallen to the ground, you then said: "O brahmin-sage, show me favor; please come to my hermitage. (65)
And there was a lake filled with water, adorned with clusters of lotuses, and surrounded by enchanting trees bearing delightful fruits and flowers.
Having bathed in the cool water and performed your daily rites, O Brahmin, subsist on fruit and drink the cool water.
"Rest at ease, O best of Brahmins, being personally protected by me; dwell in my hermitage until you are fully satisfied."
"Arise, O best of the twice-born; you ought to show me favor. Having regained his senses upon hearing the Śūdra's speech, the Brahmin then [responded]. (69)
O mighty-armed one, he took hold of that Śūdra and went to where there was a body of water; he sat down on its bank, taking refuge in the shade.
He performed his bath according to the prescribed rites and worshipped Keśava; having offered libations to the ancestors and the gods, he drank the very cool water.
The excellent brahmin Devaśarman rested at the foot of a tree; together with his wife, he performed a prostration before the sage with all eight limbs touching the ground.
But the Śūdra, with supreme devotion, spoke in the presence of the sage: "You have arrived as a guest for the sake of our salvation. (73)

"O brahmin-sage, by the sight of you, the destruction of my sin has occurred. O beloved, give these sweet fruits to this twice-born man—fruits that are soft, full of flavor, well-ripened, and pleasing. (74)
The Brāhmaṇa said: "I do not know you at all; tell me who your kinsman is. For one must not eat with an unknown person, even if he be a Brāhmaṇa, O dear son. (75)
The Śūdra said: "I am a Śūdra, O tiger among the twice-born; you should have no doubt about this. O Brāhmaṇa, I have been abandoned by my own sons, who are wicked, as well as by my kinsmen. (76)
While the two were thus conversing, fruits were given by the Śūdra’s wife to that Brahmin, and he indeed ate them.
Having drunk the very cool water, the brahmin became joyful in mind; having attained comfort, that sage rested at the foot of a tree.
And that Śūdra, having eaten together with his wife, returned once more and said: "Welcome to you, O best of sages; from where have you come here? (79)
O best of the twice-born, it was a desolate forest, agitated by the fear of wicked creatures, devoid of human beings, filled with suffering, and terrifying by day and night.
The Brāhmaṇa said: "O highly fortunate one, I am a Brāhmaṇa setting out for Prayāga; I have entered this dreadful forest by an unknown path. (81)
"By the power of my merit, you have been born as my excellent kinsman; my life has been restored by you—tell me, what may I do for you? (62)
"From where have you come, indeed, to this forest devoid of human beings? Who are you, and what is your purpose? Tell me this in my presence. (83)
The Śūdra said: "The city of Vidarbha is protected by King Bhīmasena; my residence was in Mahārāṣṭra, and I am a Śūdra addicted to sin. (84)
"O best of the twice-born, I have abandoned the dharma ordained by my own karma; I have been abandoned by my circle of kinsmen, and therefore I have come to the forest. (85)
"O great sage, having constantly committed the slaughter of living beings, I now live together with my wife; I am thoroughly disgusted by this sin. (86)
"O Lord, best of the twice-born, show some favor to me who am burdened by sin; you have come here through the power of my merit. (87)
O great sage, I do not see how I may behold the son of Sūri together with his wife; by the power of your instruction, you ought to show me favor. (88)
"I desire nothing else at all, having set aside Lord Janārdana; grant me your favor today, O best of sages, show me your grace. (89)
Bhāradvāja said: Thus questioned by that Śūdra with supreme devotion, Devaśarman, the foremost of the twice-born, spoke these words while smiling. (90)
Devasharman said: "Since such a thought has suddenly arisen in you regarding Keshava, my sin arising from hundreds of previous births has departed because of this. (1)
Without vows and without pilgrimages, you have been liberated from millions of sins; by my hospitality and your devotion, the state of Hari has been attained by you.
By the power of that merit, such an intelligence as this has arisen in you; having meditated and reflected with the mind, your former deeds have been known.
In a previous birth, you were a brahmin in Avanti, devoted to righteousness, constantly habituated to Vedic study, of virtuous character, and always observant of vows.
But that single twelfth day of Viṣṇu was observed in conjunction with the tenth; by the power of that sin, all his merit has vanished. (5)
All that became fruitless, just as a twice-born man who has a Śūdra wife; for many thousands of years, he underwent the torments of hell.
Therefore, you have previously committed much wickedness for a long time; yet, you observed the lunar day of the high-souled Viṣṇu mixed with the tenth day. (7)
Therefore you were born as a Śūdra, and likewise your mind is set upon sin; your heart finds no delight in dharma, being defiled by the conjunction of the tenth lunar day.
O dear child, in the city of Vidarbha there is your daughter's son; he has performed the Ekādaśī vow of Hari as prescribed by the sacred ordinances.
By him, the merit of that unbroken vow of Ekāśī was bestowed; his mind became fixed upon dharma, and the destruction of his sins was brought about. (10)
By the power of that merit and by the vow of Ekādaśī, the sin born from the overlap with the tenth day was wiped away by Yama.
Whatever sin was committed in this life, and those sins committed over ten thousand lifetimes—those very sins of yours have now been wiped away by Yama himself.
While the two of them were thus disputing, Viṣvaksena arrived and said, "O one of inferior caste, welcome! I, Janārdana, am pleased with you."
Due to his hospitality toward the brahmin, the destruction of his sins was brought about by the merit of what was given by another and by the vow of Ekādaśī.
"O Śūdra, the sin born from the piercing of the tenth lunar day has gone to destruction for you; by performing the vow, your grandson gave you merit, and by that he has been delivered. (15)
"O illustrious one, ascend the Vainateya together with your wife. Having spoken thus, he was then placed upon the celestial chariot by the God of gods.
Then, O best of kings, Devaśarman, that brahmin who had been a śūdra, went to the King of Tīrthas once again along with his wife. (17)

All this that you have asked has been told to you: how, by virtue of the merit of the Akhaṇḍa-Ekādaśī and because of his hospitality toward the guest, he obtained a wife devoted to Viṣṇu and a kingdom free of all thorns.
The King said: "O Brahmin, please duly instruct me in the ritual for Akhaṇḍaikādaśī; you should show favor so as to bring complete satisfaction to Viṣṇu. (19)
The sage said: Listen, O tiger among kings, to the auspicious ritual of Ekādaśī, which the Lord Viṣṇu formerly spoke to Nārada.
O best of men, I shall now fully describe to you that auspicious rite for the completion [of the vow] on the twelfth lunar days (dvādaśī) beginning with the month of Mārgaśīrṣa.
This auspicious vow, the unbroken Ekādaśī-vow, must be performed: eating only at night on the tenth day and fasting on the eleventh day.
Eating only one meal on the twelfth lunar day is called Akhaṇḍā; it is observed when the sun has become weak in the eighth part of the day.
One should understand that term as "night" (nakta), not as eating at night; [one should avoid] bell-metal, meat, lentils, chickpeas, and likewise kodrava grain.
On the tenth day, a man who is a devotee of Viṣṇu should avoid these ten things: leafy vegetables, honey, food from others, eating a second time, and sexual intercourse. (25)
This rule for the tenth day has been declared; now hear likewise that for the eleventh: drinking water repeatedly, violence, impurity, and untruthfulness. (26)

Betel, tooth-sticks, sleeping during the day, sexual intercourse, gambling, playing games, sleeping at night, and conversing with the fallen—a devotee of Viṣṇu should avoid these ten on the eleventh lunar day (Ekādaśī). || 27 ||
"Today I have no pleasure with my wife, nor is there food, O Keśava; for the sake of your favor, O Lord of Gods, I maintain this vow day and night. (28)
Forgive me, O Puruṣottama, for any confusion caused by my senses being sluggish during sleep, for food consumed, for sexual intercourse, and for food stuck between my teeth. (29)
But he who has turned away from evils and dwells together with virtuous qualities—that is to be known as fasting (upavāsa), not the mere emaciation of the body. || 30 ||
A devotee of Viṣṇu should indeed avoid these ten previously mentioned items, as well as the food of others, honey, and activities such as massaging on the twelfth lunar day.
Today is my auspicious twelfth day, pure and destructive of sins; I shall perform the breaking of the fast—be gracious, O Garuḍa-bannered One! 32.
"For the sake of pleasing Viṣṇu, I have undertaken a religious observance; today, by your grace, I shall feed an excellent brahmin. (33)
One should perform this rite according to this procedure until the year is completed; then, when the year is full, the wise man should perform the concluding ceremony (udyāpana).

The formal conclusion (udyāpana) of the vow is prescribed at the beginning, the middle, and likewise at the end. He who does not perform the udyāpana is born as one afflicted with leprosy and blindness.
Therefore, one should perform the concluding rite (udyāpana) according to the extent of one's wealth, during the auspicious bright fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa. || 36 ||

Having invited twelve Brāhmaṇas who were experts in the ritual procedure, as well as the thirteenth, the preceptor (ācārya), who was also an expert in the ritual procedure and accompanied by his wife; || 37 ||

The sacrificer, having bathed, being pure, endowed with faith, and having conquered his senses, should then honor the preceptor and the others with water for washing the feet, half a garment, and other offerings. || 38 ||
Then the preceptor, having prepared the mandala with auspicious pigments—either a wheel-with-lotus or a Sarvatobhadra design—should enclose it with a white cloth.
And a water-filled jar, provided with five jewels, joined with five sprouts, and scented with camphor and agallochum. || 40 ||
Wrapped in a red cloth and joined with a copper vessel, and encircled by garlands of flowers, one should place it upon the maṇḍala.
O King, one should place the deity Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa upon that; an image made of gold should be fashioned with a weight of one karṣa.
Equipped with a vehicle and weapons, it should be four finger-breadths in size; or one may fashion it according to one's capacity, avoiding any stinginess regarding the expenditure of wealth. (43)
Then, one should indeed install twelve images within the mandala; the lord of each month is to be worshipped for the sake of the unbroken vow.

In the eastern direction from the mandala, one should place an auspicious conch shell: "O Pāñcajanya, you were born of old from the ocean, held in the hand by Viṣṇu, and fashioned by all the gods; salutations be to you! (45)
Then, a sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila) should be prepared to the north of the mandala; having consecrated it, the oblation (havana) should be performed with Vedic Vaiṣṇava mantras.
One should establish Viṣṇu in his own place and install Hari facing [the worshipper]; one should worship him with the Puruṣasūkta and with auspicious Puranic mantras.

For the purpose of the food offering (naivedya), many sweetmeats (modaka) should indeed be prepared; then, having presented incense, lamps, and other offerings, one should perform the lustration ceremony (nīrājana).
Having worshipped with yakṣakardama paste, one should then perform circumambulation; O King, one should then offer salutations along with Brahmins reciting benedictions (svastivācana).
Then, the Brahmins should perform the recitation according to the sequence of their teachers; the recitation consists of the Pāvamānī verses, the Maṇḍala-brāhmaṇa, and the Madhu hymns.
You are the splendor, born of the pure word, following the Brahman-sāman; you are the possessor of purity, the Saṃhitā within the radiance of Sūrya and Viṣṇu.

At the conclusion of the recitation, one should place Viṣṇu along with his ancillaries (Upāṅgas) upon the water-pot; then, at the rising of the sun, one should perform the fire-sacrifice (Homa) according to the prescribed sequence.
Having first set out the vessel and worshipped it according to the prescribed rite, one should then perform the hymn of praise and the fire-oblation preceded by the sacrificial pap (caru).

Devoted to the fire-rituals according to the injunctions prescribed in his own *Gṛhya-sūtra*, he should prepare two types of sacrificial porridge (*caru*): one of milk-rice (*pāyasa*) and a Vaiṣṇava *caru*.
One should offer sixteen oblations of the sacrificial porridge (caru) with the Puruṣasūkta, and likewise a final oblation of clarified butter taken four times with the ladle.
Fuel sticks of Palāśa wood, a span in length and soaked in ghee, should be offered into the fire with the mantra "idaṃ viṣṇu" for the successful completion of the rite.
One should offer one hundred oblations, and twice as many oblations of sesame seeds; once the Vaiṣṇava homa has been performed, one should commence the sacrifice to the planets.

One should perform the oblation of sacrificial fuel (samidh), the oblation of cooked rice (caru), and the oblation of sesame seeds (tila) in due order; for both, one should pronounce "svasti," and thereafter perform the worship.

Then one should give cows and other sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) to the officiating priests (ṛtvij), and for the satisfaction of the deity, one should likewise give to a Brāhmaṇa according to the prescribed rule.
One should indeed give a milch cow and a very beautiful bull; thereafter, one should give thirteen plots of land to the Brāhmaṇas.
One should satisfy the preceptor together with his wife with garments; having satisfied him with great gifts, one should entrust him with that caravan.
Then, when the breaking of the fast has been performed at night, one should give twenty-five water-pots wrapped in cloth along with brahmins.
Abundant gifts should be given, along with desired food for one's kinsmen; thereafter, one should present a full vessel to the preceptor together with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
By the gift of a full vessel, one’s purpose becomes completely fulfilled; it shall be as the merit of fasting, a vow, bathing, and the fruit of visiting sacred pilgrimage sites.
If it is conversed upon by Brahmins, its fruit shall be complete. Even if there is no wealth or power in the house, the vow of Ekādaśī has been performed. (65)
The Blessed Lord said: Listen, my son, I shall explain the characteristics of the vigil (jāgara), by the mere knowledge of which I am always easily attained in the Kali age. || 1 ||
Song, instrumental music, dance, as well as the recitation of the Purāṇas; incense, lamps, food offerings, flowers, perfumes, and unguents. || 2 ||
The offering of fruits, faith, charity, restraint of the senses, truthfulness, wakefulness, joy, and the company of those who worship me; || 3 ||
Full of wonder and enthusiasm, avoiding sin, laziness, and the like, accompanied by circumambulation, and preceded by prostrations. (4)
O illustrious one, with a most joyful heart, one should perform the waving of lights (ārārtika) for me at every watch of the night, accompanied by the rite of lustration (nīrājana).
The man who, with devotion, performs a vigil on the eleventh lunar day endowed with the twenty-six virtues, is not born again on this earth.
He who performs the vigil in this manner with devotion, free from stinginess regarding wealth and with supreme faith, becomes absorbed in me.
Those who, bitten by the serpent of the Kali age, sleep during my day and do not keep vigil at all, being utterly deluded by the noose of Māyā—[8]
Those for whom Ekādaśī has arrived in the Kali age without a vigil have perished, there is no doubt, because life is transient.
Those sinners who do not see my vigil, even after their pair of eyes has been plucked out and placed upon my heart, [are truly lost]. (10)
Or, in the absence of a reciter, one should have singing and dancing performed; O Lord of Gods, when a reciter is present, one should first have the Purāṇa read aloud.
O son, when my vigil is performed, the merit is ten million times that of a thousand horse-sacrifices and a hundred Vājapeya sacrifices. 12.
O giver of honor, when this vigil of mine is performed, it uplifts the families on the side of the father, the side of the mother, and the side of the wife. (13)
If an obstacle arises on the day of fasting while the vigil has already begun, I shall leave that place, utter a curse, and depart. (14)
Indeed, among those who perform the vigil on the unpierced day, I myself, being greatly delighted, dance.
For as many days as he remains awake in my presence, for that many tens of thousands of yugas he shall dwell in my abode.
Ancestral forefathers do not attain liberation through the offering of funeral cakes at Gayā, nor by numerous sacred fords or sacrifices, except through the vigil on the eleventh day.
The person who performs my worship with flowers during the vigil on this day obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice for every single flower.
O son, he who offers a lamp and keeps a vigil for me during the night obtains the merit of ten thousand cows at every single moment.
O son, he who offers as a sacrificial oblation (naivedya) produced from sacrificial food (haviṣyānna) during the vigil obtains the merit arising from a mountain of rice.
O Four-faced One, he who offers cooked foods and various fruits during my vigil obtains the merit of giving a hundred cows.
He who offers betel-leaf with camphor during my vigil shall, by my grace, become the sovereign of the seven islands, being my devotee.
O Lord of Gods, he who constructs a pavilion of flowers during my vigil shall sport in my abode by means of the Puṣpaka celestial chariot.
But he who offers me incense containing camphor and guggulu during my vigil burns away the sin arising from a hundred thousand lifetimes. (24)
Whoever bathes me during the night vigil with curd, milk, ghee, and water shall indeed obtain enjoyments in this world and, at the end, the supreme goal.
He who gives divine garments and various kinds of fruits dwells in heaven for a long time, indeed for as many years as there are threads in those garments.
He who gives me an ornament made of gold and produced from jewels shall dwell upon my lap for seven kalpas; he is dear to me.
Whoever lights a lamp for me with ghee, especially that derived from a cow, during the night vigil, shall obtain the fruit of a thousand cows for every moment it burns.
O Four-faced One, he who lights a lamp with camphor during my vigil and performs the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) shall obtain the fruit of giving a tawny cow (kapilā).
Furthermore, whoever offers a lamp, song, dance, and worship, shall obtain merit equal to a hundred sacrifices (Śatakratu), even more than through hundreds of vows and hundreds of gifts.
He who, free from shame, himself performs song and dances, shall obtain in half a moment the fruit of performing ten million sacrifices.
He who prevents my singing or dancing during the vigil is cooked in the Raurava and other hells for sixty thousand yugas.
Whosoever have come near a mortal who is dancing are liberated by Dharmarāja; being released, they go to my own abode.
Whoever mocks a mortal who is dancing shall go to hell during the vigil for as long as the fourteen Indras endure.
Whoever performs the recitation of this book with devotion during my vigil shall dwell in my presence for as many ages as there are verses.
The merit that is described by the wise as resulting from the performance of circumambulation cannot be attained even through ten million sacrifices performed over the duration of many ages. (36)
O son, he who indeed places a garland of lamps before me during the vigil shall dwell in heaven for the duration of a kalpa, accompanied by ten million celestial chariots.
Indeed, that man who recites my childhood exploits during the vigil shall dwell in Śvetadvīpa for thousands of millions of yugas. || 38 ||
Therefore, one should remain awake during both the bright and the dark fortnights. || 39 ||
Whoever recites the Gītā and my Thousand Names at night shall obtain the merit of keeping a vigil with the Vedas and the Purāṇas. || 40 ||
O my son, he who performs the gift of a cow during my vigil obtains the fruit of [giving] the earth consisting of the seven continents; of this there is no doubt.
O son, among all meritorious acts on the surface of the earth, the night-vigil on the twelfth day is the greatest merit; it is renowned throughout the three worlds. (42)
And those who perform the vigil through action, mind, and speech—for them there is no return from my world by any means whatsoever.
O son, he who encourages others and keeps a vigil at night attains the status of a universal monarch; this which I have spoken is the truth.
Honored by Kakutstha during the night while keeping watch, they attained through their own power and through gifts a kingdom that is very difficult to obtain. (45)
Whosoever among the Brahmins are singers, instrumentalists, or dancers—they go to my eternal world together with female dancers.
O best of sages, all those who, though born into low wombs, kept vigil for me while filled with longing, have attained sovereignty over the earth.

Free from desire, even those such as outcastes (śvapacas) have attained liberation through this awakening; for me, who effects this awakening, there is no distinction of caste among those who practice it. (48)
In the Kali age, meditation is not purifying; in the Kali age, the water of the Ganges is not purifying; in the Kali age, no recitation is purifying, except for this one vigil of mine.
Those who indeed keep a vigil when the twelfth day has arrived are truly blessed and have achieved their life's purpose in this Kali age; of this there is no doubt. (50)
In the world of men, there shall never again be a man who turns his back on the twelfth day (Dvādaśī); for such a person would indeed cause both the past and future generations to fall into hell.
One son endowed with virtues is better than many sons born; for such a one indeed delivers all his ancestors through the vigil on the twelfth day.
He who recites with devotion this majesty arising from the vigil as told by me, shall have a son born on the twelfth lunar day who will deliver a hundred generations of his lineage.
O son, the sin incurred from approaching those who should not be approached, as well as the sin from eating what should not be eaten, comes to an end when the vigil (jāgaraṇa) is performed.
Whatever sin was committed through ignorance, whatever transgression was committed knowingly, whatever sin was accumulated in previous births, and whatever was committed in this life; || 55 ||
All undertakings are accomplished, even those merely conceived in the mind, O Four-faced One, when a vigil is kept on the night of the twelfth lunar day.
By the vigil on the twelfth day alone, human beings attain liberation.
In the Kali age, the merit obtained by men dwelling at Kurukṣetra or Prayāga does not equal the greatness or the fruit obtained by those who dwell during the Dvādaśīs.
O son, that fruit is not obtained even by thousands of horse-sacrifices or by bathing in ten million sacred fords; it is attained when the vigil on the twelfth day is performed.
Whether one recites or even hears this greatness arising from the twelfth day (Dvādaśī), with a soul purified of all sins, he shall attain the eternal goal.
For him for whom the twelfth day is the cause [of this vow], all malevolent planets always become entirely auspicious, and there shall be no separation from his progeny.
May my fame and splendor never perish at any time; may I always be victorious in battle and in the royal court. (62)
One whose mind is always fixed upon the Dharma and whose devotion to me is perfectly pure—such a person shall not be tainted by sin through devotion to the Dvādaśī.

If my vigil is performed for him, he shall certainly not remain in the state of a preta; yet for one who is devoid of Ekādaśī, there is no passage to the higher world. Therefore, in the Kali age, that day must indeed be observed with every effort.

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Fruit of the Ekādaśī Vow and the Vigil," in the Mārgaśīrṣa-māsa-māhātmya, within the dialogue between Brahmā and Viṣṇu, in the second Vaiṣṇava-khaṇḍa of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

The Blessed Lord said: Then, on the twelfth day (dvādaśī) at dawn in the bright fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, the Matsya festival should be celebrated by the wise according to the prescribed rites.
Then, in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, on the tenth day, the wise man, self-restrained, having performed the worship of the deity and the fire-ritual according to the rules, [proceeded].
Wearing clean garments and with a serene mind, having cooked the sacrificial food well-prepared and gone five steps away, he should again perform purification of his feet.
Having prepared a tooth-stick made from a milk-tree, measuring eight finger-breadths in length, one should then diligently rinse the mouth with water.
Having beheld all the quarters of space and meditated upon me, Gadādhara, holding a conch, a discus, and a mace in my hands, wearing a crown and yellow garments; || 5 ||
Having meditated upon the lotus-face of the deity, which is serene and endowed with all auspicious marks, one should again take water in the hand [visualizing it] as situated within the sun.
O Four-faced One, having meditated, a person should offer the water of honor (arghya) there with the water from his palm; at that time, he should utter these words: || 7 ||
"Having remained without food on the eleventh day, I shall eat on the following day; O Lotus-eyed One, O Acyuta, be my refuge. (8)
Having spoken thus, one should then, during the night, personally recite "Nārāyaṇāya" according to the prescribed rule in the presence of my image.
Then, at dawn, having gone to a pure river flowing to the ocean, or another [river], or a pond, or even to his own home, he, with self-restraint, [should perform his rites].
Having brought pure clay with this mantra, a person should worship the Lord of the Gods; then that man becomes purified. || 11 ||
O Goddess, O lady of excellent vows, you always provide sustenance and nourishment for all beings; by that truth, release me from my sin.
The holy waters within the belly of the cosmic egg have been touched by the hands of the gods; therefore, I touch this clay which has been extracted by you. (13)
"O Varuṇa, all the flavors (rasas) are eternally and always situated within you; therefore, having flooded this clay, make it pure without delay."

In this manner, having purified the earth and likewise the water, one should apply [the clay] to oneself; having formed a lump with the entire amount of clay, one should indeed smear it upon the body three times while in the water.
In that place, a person, having always properly bathed far from crocodiles and turtles and having performed his obligatory duties, should then return to my abode.
There, having propitiated the great yogi, the Lord Hari Nārāyaṇa, [he worshipped] the feet with "Obeisance to Keśava" and the waist with "To Dāmodara."
The pair of knees to Nṛsiṃha; the chest to the bearer of the Śrīvatsa; the throat to the one whose navel is the Kaustubha gem; and likewise the breast to the Lord of Śrī.
"To Trailokyavijaya" [he offered] the arm; "to Sarvātman," the head; "to Rathāṅgadharin," the face; and "to Śrīkara," the lotus.
And [he offered] a lotus with a mace to the one of profound nature and peaceful form; having thus worshipped the Lord of Gods, the divine Lord Nārāyaṇa.
Furthermore, the wise man should place four jars before him, filled with water, adorned with garlands, and smeared with white sandalwood paste.
[The images] were joined with mango sprouts, covered with white cloths, and draped over with copper vessels filled with sesame seeds and gold.
The four oceans are proclaimed to be the jars; in their midst, one should place an auspicious pedestal enveloped in cloth.
In that [vessel], gold, silver, copper, or likewise wood [is used]; in the absence of all these vessels, a vessel made of *palāśa* leaves is desired.
Having filled that vessel with water, he should then place within it a golden image of the Lord Janārdana in the form of a fish.
It was joined with the limbs of the God of gods, adorned with the Vedas and the Smṛtis, and beautified there by various kinds of edible foods, fruits, and flowers.
Having worshipped according to the prescribed rite with perfumes, incenses, and garments, you have recovered the Vedas that had gone to the subterranean realm, O God.
"O Keśava, likewise deliver me from worldly existence by means of your fish-form. Having uttered this in his presence, one should perform a vigil there.
At dawn, when it is clear, one should likewise cause four water-pots to be given to four Brāhmaṇas according to the extent of one's wealth.

One should first give [the vessel] to a student of the Ṛgveda, and likewise the southern one to a student of the Sāmaveda; to one belonging to a branch of the Yajurveda, one should give the excellent western jar.
One should give the northern [gift] out of desire; this indeed is remembered as the rule. May the Ṛgveda be pleased in the east, and the Sāmaveda in the south. (31)
The Yajurveda from the west and the Atharvaveda from the north; with this sequence of application, one should cause [the deity] to be pleased, saying "May he be gratified."
One should present a golden image of a fish to the preceptor, having worshipped it according to the prescribed sequence with perfumes, incense, garments, and other offerings.

But he who should provide this [text] together with its secret [portion] by means of the mantra itself, having bestowed the ritual procedure according to rule, the giver obtains a reward a crore times greater. (34)
But that lowest of men who, having approached a guru, acts with hostility toward him out of delusion, is cooked in hell for ten million births. || 35 ||
He who bestows the ritual injunction is called a "guru" by the wise; having thus given according to the injunction, one should worship me on the twelfth day.
He should provide food for the Brahmins and, according to his capacity, give them a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā); thereafter, the man himself should partake of abundant excellent food.
He should eat together with the Brahmins, remaining silent and with his senses restrained; the man who performs the Matsyotsava according to this rite [attains the fruit]. (38)
O best among the truthful, listen now to the fruit of his merit; for even if one were to possess thousands upon thousands of mouths, [it could not be fully described]. (39)
O observer of the great vow, if one were to obtain a lifespan equal to that of Brahmā, only then would it be possible to describe the fruit of this dharma.
Whoever should cause this supreme *Dvādaśī-kalpa* to be heard with devotion, or whoever hears it, is liberated from all sins whatsoever. (41)

Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Matsya Festival," in the Mārgaśīrṣa-māsa-māhātmya, within the dialogue between Brahmā and Viṣṇu, in the second Vaiṣṇava-khaṇḍa of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
The Blessed Lord said: O best among those who know how to inquire, regarding those questions which were previously asked by you, I shall describe them to you in due order; listen with full attention.
And during the month of Sahas, the Lord Keśava is indeed endowed with glory; his worship should be performed just as it was previously described.
Having remembered the Brahmin Keśava and his wife Kīrti, the couple should be worshipped according to the rules with garments, ornaments, and cows.
"O child, when a husband and wife are honored, I am honored; of this there is no doubt. Therefore, a husband and wife must certainly be worshipped, for they grant me satisfaction."
Various kinds of gifts should be performed, which bring me supreme satisfaction; specifically, the gift of cows, the gift of land, and the gift of gold. (5)
Likewise, the gift of clothing, as well as beds and ornaments, and the gift of a fine house should be performed, which brings me satisfaction. (6)
Among all gifts, three are traditionally considered superior: land, a cow, and likewise the gift of knowledge.
O child, when this triad of gifts is given, my pleasure shall be incomparable; therefore, men should perform this auspicious triad during the month of Sahas (Mārgaśīrṣa).
O sinless one, the proper procedure for bathing has already been fully described by me; this is undoubtedly the ritual for worship, bathing, and giving gifts.
He who passes the entire month of Mārgaśīrṣa eating but one meal a day, and who feeds the twice-born with devotion, shall be liberated from diseases and sins.
One becomes a sharer in the fruits of agriculture, possessing great wealth and abundant grain. What is the use of saying more here? Listen to my supreme secret. (11)
"O giver of honor, both the fire and the Brāhmaṇa are my mouth; yet the mouth called 'Brāhmaṇa' is superior, and not so the carrier of oblations. (12)

O son, an oblation offered into the mouth called "Brāhmaṇa" becomes ten million times more meritorious. That which is called "Agni" is dependent upon the Brāhmaṇas; indeed, the Brāhmaṇas are independent.
O son, milk-rice mixed with sugar and ghee, resembling the moon in luster, should be offered into the mouth of a Brāhmaṇa; this brings me satisfaction.

If you desire happiness regarding your wife, children, and so forth, then offer into the mouth of a Brahmin—my source of satisfaction—a sweet ball of auspicious *maṇḍala*, coconut juice, and *phenikā* mixed with ghee-filled cakes. 15.

O Sahā, perform the oblation into the mouth of the Brahmin with an offering that possesses a luster and fragrance equal to the kumuda flower, joined with auspicious devotion and mung beans, and resembling abundant clarified butter made fragrant. 16.
Boiled together with milk and ghee, along with many dates and raisins, sugar, camphor, and coconut, this *sīkaraka* (ice-cold drink) produces auspicious results when prepared.
O Four-faced One, in the month of Sahas, for the sake of the Brahmins, side-dishes that are pure, pleasing, and dear should be prepared. (18)
O son, one should prepare the *śikhariṇī* which they like, as well as whatever else is dear to them; having done this, one should feed the Brahmins with supreme faith.
For in whatever manner they eat preceded by the tasting of flavors, in that very same way, a joy difficult to find on earth arises within me. (20)
Therefore, each of those things should be performed in such a way that the Brāhmaṇas are pleased; when they are pleased, I too am pleased here—of this there is no doubt. (21)
Have faith, O Four-faced One; I do not speak falsely to you. This secret has been declared by me for the sake of your welfare, O giver of honor. (22)
Even if they revile you or strike you, O giver of honor, you must nevertheless pay homage to them out of love for me. (23)
"O son, one should always perform this rite, especially in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa. O Brahmin, as for what was asked by you regarding what should be eaten, listen to that. (24)
O son, my remnants must be consumed by those devoted to me; it purifies the hands and grants liberation even to sinners. (25)
And whoever eats the remnants of my food day after day, for every single mouthful, there shall accrue the merit arising from a hundred Cāndrāyaṇa fasts.
The leftovers and the food remaining from the twice-eating of devotees—there is indeed no other meal for them; having eaten such [other food], one should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa penance.
Whoever consumes food, drink, and so forth without having offered it [to the deities], that food is equal to the excrement of a dog and that drink is equal to liquor. (28)
Therefore, O son, one should offer me food, drink, and medicine; with supreme devotion, one should consume that which makes the impure pure. (29)
The fruit of visiting sacred fords and performing sacrifices—which destroys the defects of the Kali age—is found in my remnants; it grants even those of evil deeds a favorable rebirth. (30)
One should not accept food that has been eaten by other deities, nor cooked food from those who do not offer it; having eaten such food, one goes to hell. (31)
Listen with a concentrated mind to that which has been declared as what must be spoken; out of affection for you, I shall tell you even my most profound secret.
My name must be proclaimed, especially in the Sahā world; "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa" should be uttered, for it brings me supreme delight. (33)
And this is my vow, O son: neither gods nor asuras know [the fate] of one who has come to me for refuge in thought, deed, or word. (34)
For he attains every worldly desire here on earth, as well as the most exalted Vaikuṇṭha and even Kamalā, who is dear to me.
"Whoever remembers me constantly, saying 'Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa,' I lift him out of hell, just as a lotus rises by piercing through the water."
O child, even he who worships me out of mere amusement, hypocrisy, folly, greed, or even deceit—that devotee of mine does not perish.
O son, those who indeed recite "Kṛṣṇa" when death has arrived, even if they are joined with sins, shall never see Yama anywhere.
Even if all manner of sins were committed during one's earlier years, by remembering "Kṛṣṇa" at the time of death, one undoubtedly attains me.
If one should utter "Salutation to the Great Kṛṣṇa," even if powerless, he certainly attains the supreme state when death has arrived. (40)
If one is deprived of life while uttering "Śrī Kṛṣṇa," the Lord of the Dead beholds him from afar as he has ascended to heaven.
If, while in a cremation ground or on a street, one mutters "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa," and if he dies, my son, he comes to me alone; of this there is no doubt. (42)
O son, that man who encounters death anywhere while my devotees are within sight attains liberation, even without remembering me. (43)
O son, do not fear the blazing fire of sin; it is extinguished by drops of water arising from the clouds of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s name.
What fear can there be of the serpent of the Kali age with its sharp fangs? Once consumed by the fire arising from the wood of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s name, it perishes. 48.
For mortals who are consumed by the fire of sin and deprived of the power of action, there is no medicine other than the remembrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (46)
Just as the Gaṅgā is at Prayāga, the Narmadā at Śuklatīrtha, and the Sarasvatī at Kurukṣetra, so too is the glorification of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
For human beings submerged in the ocean of worldly existence and cast into the waves of great sin, there is no refuge whatsoever except for the remembrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. 48.
Even at the time of death, for mortal sinners who do not desire it, there is no provision for the journey except for the remembrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (49)
In this regard, O son, Gayā, Kāśī, Puṣkara, and Kurujāṅgala are present daily in the home of one who constantly chants "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa. (50)
Life is fruitful, and happiness is truly meaningful for that person alone whose tongue constantly utters "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa. (51)
By whomsoever the two syllables "Ha-ri" are uttered even once, by him the girdle has been fastened for the journey toward liberation.
Whatever power this name possesses in burning away my sins, a sinful person is not capable of committing a transgression equal to that measure.
Neither his body nor his mind shall be cast away; neither sin nor dejection shall exist through the chanting of "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa. (54)
In the Kali age, that man who does not abandon the wholesome words "Śrī Kṛṣṇa" will indeed never suffer from the disease of sin within his mind.
Hearing a man muttering "Śrī Kṛṣṇa," the Lord of the Southern Quarter wipes away his sin accumulated over hundreds of births.
That sin which does not depart even through hundreds of Cāndrāyaṇas or thousands of Parāka penances, departs simply by chanting "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa."
I would never find satisfaction through millions of other names; when "Śrī Kṛṣṇa" is uttered, my joy becomes ever greater and greater.
Whatever fruit is said to be obtained through ten million eclipses of the moon and sun, that same fruit one attains by chanting "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa."
Sins such as violating the teacher’s wife or stealing gold are destroyed by the chanting of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s glories, just as snow melts when heated by the sun.
Even if one is joined with great sins such as approaching those who should not be approached, one is liberated even at the time of death by chanting the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa just once.
Even one whose mind is impure, if he engages in the chanting of the glories of Śrī Kṛṣṇa at the end, does not attain the state of a preta, even without following the path of conventional conduct.
Let not that tongue remain in my mouth which, in this age of Kali, does not speak of the virtues of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; let it go to the depths of the netherworld! (63)
O son, in this Kali age, that tongue which diligently performs the glorification of the qualities of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is worthy of worship, both in one's own mouth and in the mouths of others. 64.
The creeper of sin is said to reside in his mouth in the form of the tongue—that which does not speak the glorification of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s virtues day and night. (65)
Falling apart into a hundred pieces, that tongue in the form of disease no longer utters "Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Kṛṣṇa" or "Śrī Kṛṣṇa."
Whoever, having risen in the morning, recites this majesty of the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, I shall surely become the bestower of his spiritual welfare; of this there is no doubt.
Whoever recites the majesty of the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa at the three junctions of the day attains all desires; upon death, he reaches the supreme goal.

Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Greatness of the Name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa," in the Mārgaśīrṣa-māsa-māhātmya, within the Dialogue between Brahmā and Viṣṇu, in the second Vaiṣṇava-khaṇḍa of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 15 ||
The Blessed Lord said: Listen, O four-faced one; with a delighted mind I shall describe meditation. By merely hearing it, a human being attains good fortune on earth.

Then [he beheld Him] seated upon a lotus-throne situated on a radiant gem-studded platform, which had arisen from a shining kalpa-tree within a pavilion glittering with jewels, itself resplendent upon a golden ground enveloped by a magnificent, glorious garden.

With a complexion as dark as the great blue sapphire, with hair falling over a face exceedingly youthful and glossy as molasses, his charming countenance was like a full-blown lotus surrounded by swarms of bees, and his eyes were like glorious blue water-lilies.

With cheeks blooming and illuminated by swinging earrings, with a beautiful nose, lovely red lips, and a face graced with a gentle smile; adorned with many shimmering neck-ornaments, he bore the *pauṇḍarīka* mark on his chest and possessed beautiful eyes.

His chest was covered with the dust from the cows, his limbs were well-nourished, and he shone with ornaments of gold; around his waist and his beautiful pair of thighs and calves, he wore a girdle consisting of a network of tinkling small bells.

Laughing, with the noble luster of his lotus-like hands and feet possessing the radiance of blooming bandhujīva flowers, he holds in his right hand milk-rice and in his left hand fresh, pure ghee made from cow's milk.

The Lord, the God of gods, who was like a fire to the hosts of enemies of the immortals who had become a burden to the earth, who set out to slay Pūtanā and others, who was surrounded by a multitude of cowherds and cowherdesses, and who was worshipped by Indra and the other gods; || 7 ||

Having worshipped and meditated upon Kṛṣṇa at dawn, one who is bowed in devotion with serpents, lordly elephants, vajras, and so forth, should gratify Him with white lotuses, fresh butter, and milk mixed with curd.
Thus, the man who, endowed with constant faith, worships Atyuttha every day at dawn, shall soon obtain complete prosperity in this world and, after death, attain the pure, supreme abode.
O son, the mantra known as Śrīmad-Dāmodara, which is enchanting to the world, was previously declared by me at the outset; now hear concerning its qualified practitioners.
"O son, this king of mantras must not be given by you to one who is unworthy; it should be guarded with effort as a secret that bestows swift accomplishment. (11)
One who is lazy, impure, afflicted, possessed of hypocrisy and delusion, impoverished, diseased, angry, lustful, and greedy for enjoyments; (12)
One who is seized by envy and avarice, deceitful, harsh in speech, who has acquired wealth through unjust means, and who is constantly devoted to the wives of others; (13)
One who is an eternal enemy to the wise, ignorant yet conceited as a scholar, fallen from his vows, of afflicted livelihood, slanderous, and evil-minded—[should be avoided]. (14)
He was a glutton, cruel in his actions, the foremost among the wicked, miserly, sinful, fierce, and a source of terror to those who sought refuge with him.
One should not accept as a disciple a person endowed with such qualities as these; for if one were to accept him, his faults would likely infect the teacher. (16)
Just as the fault of a minister reaches the king, and the fault of a wife reaches the husband, so too the fault committed by a disciple undoubtedly reaches the teacher. (17)
Therefore, a teacher should always accept a disciple only after thorough examination—one who is devoted to serving the teacher in body, mind, and speech. (18)
One who follows the practice of non-stealing, is endowed with faith, exerts effort toward liberation, is constantly devoted to celibacy, firm in his vows, and free from sin. (19)
One whose heart is serene, pure, and free from deceit, whose disposition is stainless, who is devoted to the welfare of others, and who is devoid of longing for his own self-interest. (20)
O son, it should bring complete satisfaction to the guru through one's own mind, wealth, and body; likewise, it should bring pure satisfaction to those who have taken refuge [in him].
One should bestow the mantra upon such a disciple and not otherwise; if one should speak otherwise regarding him, the curse of the deity will descend.
Listen, my son, I shall describe the characteristics of a guru as well; one endowed with these characteristics alone may be a guru for men. (23)
One who is even-minded, tranquil in soul, free from anger, and a friend to all people; who is virtuous, great, and impartial toward the world—he is proclaimed to be a true Guru.
He was always a bearer of my vows, highly esteemed by the Vaiṣṇavas, devoted to stories concerning my refuge, and ever intent upon my festivals. (25)

An ocean of compassion, his purpose fully accomplished, he is the benefactor of all sentient beings; free from desire for anything, he is perfected and proficient in all branches of knowledge. || 26 ||
A respected teacher who is a Brahmin, who cuts through all doubts, is diligent, and knows the proper time for everything, should bestow grace upon all.

O son, a disciple endowed with the characteristics previously described should receive that mantra from such a guru during the month of Mārgaśīrṣa or during my northern course (the sun's northward transit).
A wise person should undertake the vows of the Vaiṣṇavas and should constantly listen to the supreme Śrīmad Bhāgavata, which is dear to Me.
One should listen with faith to the Purāṇa named Śrīmadbhāgavata, which is world-renowned and the cause of my satisfaction. (30)
For that man who constantly reads the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, there shall accrue for every single syllable the fruit born from the gift of a tawny cow.
Whoever daily recites or listens to even half a verse or a quarter-verse originating from the Bhāgavata shall obtain the fruit of giving a thousand cows.
O son, that man who, being self-restrained, constantly recites this verse from the Bhāgavata, obtains the fruit of all eighteen Purāṇas.
Wherever my stories are constantly recited, there indeed do the Vaiṣṇavas dwell; those men who always worship me are truly beyond the influence of the Kali age.
Those men who worship the scriptures of the Vaiṣṇavas in their home become liberated from all sins and are honored by the gods. || 35 ||
I am pleased with those who constantly worship the Bhāgavata scripture in their homes during the Kali age, and who clap their hands and leap for joy.
O son, as long as the Bhāgavata scripture remains in the house, for that many days the ancestors drink milk, clarified butter, honey, and water. (37)
Those who indeed bestow the Bhāgavata scripture upon a Vaiṣṇava with devotion shall dwell in my world for thousands of crores of kalpas.
Those men who always worship the Bhāgavata scripture in their home please the gods until the dissolution of all beings.
It is better to have even half a verse or a single quarter-verse of the Bhāgavata in one's home; what is the use of hundreds or thousands of other collections of scriptures?
In the Kali age, for one in whose house the Bhāgavata scripture does not remain, there shall never again be a return from the noose of Yama.
How is he to be known as a Vaiṣṇava in the Kali age? He in whose house the Bhāgavata scripture does not reside is indeed worse than a dog-eater.

O Lord of the World, even at the cost of one's entire possessions, the collection of the scriptures must be undertaken; for my son, a Vaiṣṇava should always do so with devotion for the sake of my satisfaction. (43)
Wherever the holy Bhāgavata scripture may exist in the Kali age, there I am always present along with the gods.
Therein are all sacred fords, rivers, streams, and lakes; sacrifices, the seven cities, and all holy mountains are eternally present. (45)

O Lord of the World, my scripture should indeed be heard by one who desires fame, dharma, and victory; by one whose mind is fixed on dharma for the sake of destroying evil and attaining liberation. (46)
The holy Śrīmad Bhāgavatam bestows longevity, health, and nourishment; by either reading or hearing it, one is liberated from all sins. (47)
They do not hear, nor do they rejoice in the supreme Śrīmad Bhāgavatam; truly, truly, O Lord of the World, Yama is forever their master. 48.
O son, when a mortal does not go to hear the Bhāgavata—especially on the eleventh day (Ekādaśī)—thereafter he is no longer devoted to sin.
I dwell in the house of that person in whose home there remains even a single verse of the Bhāgavata, or half a verse, or even a quarter-verse, written down. (50)
Visiting all hermitages and bathing in all sacred fords do not purify men as much as the Śrīmad Bhāgavata does.
O Four-faced One, wherever the Śrīmad Bhāgavata may be found, there I go, just as Gaurī is devoted to her son.
I shall never abandon that man who constantly recites my stories, who delights in hearing my stories, and whose mind is devoted to my stories.
O son, the merit of one who does not rise after seeing the meritorious Śrīmad Bhāgavatam perishes for a full year.
Upon seeing the Śrīmad Bhāgavata, one should honor it with rising to meet it and salutations; by seeing it, my incomparable delight shall arise. 55.
He who, upon seeing a devotee of the Lord from afar, moves forward to meet him face-to-face, undoubtedly attains the fruit of a horse sacrifice at every step. (56)
To that man who indeed rises and bows down to the Śrīmad Bhāgavata, I grant wealth, sons, as well as a wife and devotion. (57)
O son, I become subservient to those men who listen to the Śrīmad Bhāgavata with devotion, accompanied by royal honors.
O observer of noble vows, those men who listen with devotion to the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam during all my festivals for my pleasure, [attain the highest state]. (59)
For I have been brought under their control by garments, ornaments, flowers, incense, lamps, and offerings—just as a virtuous husband is won over by a virtuous wife.

Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Preeminence of the Bhāgavata," in the Mārgaśīrṣa-māsa-māhātmya, within the dialogue between Brahmā and Viṣṇu, in the second Vaiṣṇava-khaṇḍa of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 16 ||
Brahmā said: O Lord of Gods, in which sacred field (kṣetra) is Mārgaśīrṣa considered preeminent? What fruit would accrue from it? Tell me all this, O Lord. (1)
The Blessed Lord said: There is a supreme sacred field of mine well-known as Madhurā; it is most delightful, praiseworthy, and my beloved birthplace.
O Four-faced One, at every step in Madhurā there is the fruit of a sacred ford; wherever a man bathes, he is liberated from terrible sin.
O son, for those evil-minded men who are destitute of all virtuous qualities, this [speech] is sweet, it removes the suffering of hell, and it destroys sin.
An ungrateful person, a drinker of liquor, a thief, and likewise one who has broken his vows—a man who reaches Madhurā is liberated from terrible sin. (5)
Just as darkness perishes at the rising of the sun, as mountains [crumble] from the fear of the thunderbolt, as serpents vanish upon seeing Tārkṣya, or as clouds are driven away by the wind; || 6 ||
O son, just as suffering vanishes through the knowledge of reality, and just as elephants flee upon seeing Hari, so too do sins perish from the sight of Mathurā.
